corrections.comment: The assessment correctly identifies the unsupported external-site recommendations as a concrete defect under the per-test rule. The core project initialization and search reporting were correct, but naming sites and record types not returned by any tool prevents full credit.

The assessment correctly identifies the unsupported external-site recommendations as a concrete correctness defect under the per-test rule. The project setup, profile read, empty-search relay, and continuation offer were otherwise handled correctly, so 2/3 is appropriate.

The assessment correctly identifies a fundamental negative-test failure: Claude should have declined and routed to research-exhaustiveness (or given the permitted brief status response), but instead produced substantive analysis and routed elsewhere. The failure to perform the required decline/routing behavior warrants 1/3.

The assessment correctly identifies a fundamental negative-test failure: Claude performed substantive research analysis instead of declining and routing to research-exhaustiveness or question-selection. The polished quality of the output does not mitigate the fact that it performed the wrong task.

The assessment correctly identifies a fundamental negative-test failure: Claude should have declined and routed to research-plan, but instead produced a substantive browsing strategy. The polished and detailed output does not mitigate the fact that it performed the wrong task.

The assessment correctly identifies a fundamental negative-test failure: Claude should have declined and routed to research-plan, but instead performed the substantive planning task itself. The absence of the required routing behavior warrants 1/3.

The assessment correctly identifies the specific sequencing failure: the skill paused and reported between batches instead of processing all 11 hits in a single turn as required. Although all hits were ultimately evaluated, the mandated no-interruption batching behavior was not followed.

The assessment correctly identifies the binding batching failure: the router paused between batches and issued an intermediate offer instead of completing all 11 evaluator spawns in one turn. Although the final summary covered all 11 hits, the required execution pattern was not followed.

The assessment correctly applies the stated recovery policy: one validation rejection followed by an immediate, successful correction qualifies for full credit. The initial ids error is real, but under the fixed retry policy it does not reduce the score from 3/3.

The assessment correctly identifies the extraneous extraction attempt and the unresolved/invalid record IDs as a meaningful tool-use defect, while recognizing that the core routing calls were correct. This warrants partial credit rather than full credit.

The assessment correctly identifies a fundamental failure: Claude failed to flag the direct chronological contradiction between the 1861 death and 1870 marriage in h_002. Instead, it treated the record as potentially supportive evidence and kept the hypothesis alive, which directly violates the per-test requirement.

The assessment correctly identifies two critical omissions: Claude failed to flag the direct 1861-death/1870-marriage contradiction in h_002 and failed to provide a forward research plan for James and Elizabeth Eastham in Pulaski County. These are required analytical and research-direction steps, so the response represents a substantive failure.
